#+TITLE: PRoot Apps

# This file is generated from ci-scripts/README.template and metadata/metadata.yml, edit those instead

A [[https://github.com/linuxserver/proot-apps][PRoot Apps]] repository laid out like linuxserver/proot-apps. A
[[https://github.com/selkies-project/sealskin][SealSkin]] PRoot Apps catalog can use it as a remote by its GitHub ~owner/repo~.

* Supported Apps

| Name | Full Endpoint | Category | Arch | Description |
|------+---------------+----------+------+-------------|
| emacs | ghcr.io/queitsch/proot-apps:emacs | Development | linux/amd64,linux/arm64 | GNU Emacs is an extensible, customizable, self-documenting real-time display editor. This app runs the pure GTK build natively on Wayland and switches to the GTK3 X11 build when the session has no Wayland display. |

* Adding this repository to SealSkin

In the SealSkin admin UI, open the PRoot Apps catalogs, click *New Catalog*, and
set the remote to:

#+begin_example
queitsch/proot-apps
#+end_example

SealSkin reads a GitHub ~owner/repo~ remote as
~https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<owner>/<repo>/master/metadata/metadata.yml~,
with the icons under ~metadata/img/~. It installs the first layer of the image
~ghcr.io/<owner>/<repo>:<name>~ (see ~Remote.parse~ in SealSkin's
[[https://github.com/selkies-project/sealskin/blob/main/server/app/prootapps.py][server/app/prootapps.py]]). So the metadata has to be on ~master~, and the
images have to be public on ghcr.io or pullable with the node's ghcr.io
credential.

A remote can also be a base URL and a registry, one space apart. That form
serves the metadata from any branch:

#+begin_example
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/queitsch/proot-apps/<branch> ghcr.io/queitsch/proot-apps
#+end_example

* For Users

With [[https://github.com/linuxserver/proot-apps#install-or-update][proot-apps]] installed, install, update or remove an app by its full endpoint:

#+begin_src sh
proot-apps install ghcr.io/queitsch/proot-apps:emacs
proot-apps update ghcr.io/queitsch/proot-apps:emacs
proot-apps remove ghcr.io/queitsch/proot-apps:emacs
#+end_src

** emacs

GNU Emacs from Alpine's ~emacs-pgtk~ and ~emacs-gtk3~ packages, two builds of
the same release in one app:

| Binary                         | Build          | Used when                                            |
|--------------------------------+----------------+------------------------------------------------------|
| ~/usr/bin/emacs~               | pure GTK, pgtk | the session has a Wayland socket                     |
| ~/usr/libexec/emacs-x11/emacs~ | GTK3 on X11    | there is no Wayland socket but ~DISPLAY~ is set      |

Set ~PA_EMACS_BACKEND=pgtk~ or ~PA_EMACS_BACKEND=x11~ to force a build. The
packages conflict, so the X11 binary and its fingerprinted ~.pdmp~ come from a
second build stage. Both packages ship identical Lisp. From the command line
the app is ~emacs-pa~.

* For Developers

This repository follows the build logic of [[https://github.com/linuxserver/proot-apps#for-developers][linuxserver/proot-apps]], with one
difference: the apps build on the base images that linuxserver/proot-apps
publishes (~ghcr.io/linuxserver/proot-apps:<base>~), so no base images are
built here. Set the ~BASE_REPO~ build argument to use the base images of
another repository.

- ~build-on-commit~ builds every app whose ~apps/<name>/~ folder changed on a
  push to ~master~ and pushes it to ~ghcr.io/<owner>/<repo>:<name>~ for the
  architectures in ~metadata/metadata.yml~. Run it by hand with /Build and push
  all apps/ to build everything.
- ~Daily Package check~ rebuilds each app with [[https://github.com/anchore/syft][syft]] and commits a changed
  ~apps/<name>/package_versions.txt~, which makes ~build-on-commit~ rebuild that
  app. It needs a [[https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/using-secrets-in-github-actions][GitHub Secret]] ~PAT~ with write access to the repository.
- ~template-readme~ writes this README from ~ci-scripts/README.template~ and
  ~metadata/metadata.yml~.

GitHub publishes a new container package as private, and a package does not
take on its repository's visibility ([[https://docs.github.com/en/packages/learn-github-packages/configuring-a-packages-access-control-and-visibility][docs]]). After the first build, open the
package's *Package settings* and use *Change visibility* to make it public.

** Building local apps

With Docker and proot-apps installed, build an app and extract it into your
proot-apps folder:

#+begin_src sh
./build-install-local emacs
#+end_src

** Adding a new app

Follow [[https://github.com/linuxserver/proot-apps#adding-a-new-app][Adding a new app]] in the linuxserver/proot-apps README:

1. Create ~apps/<name>/~ with ~Dockerfile~, ~entrypoint~, ~install~ and ~remove~,
   copying an existing app as a start.
2. Add the app to ~metadata/metadata.yml~ with ~name~, ~full_name~, ~arch~,
   ~category~, ~icon~ and ~description~.
3. Put its logo in ~metadata/img/~, svg preferred, otherwise a 192x192 png.
